answer.text: A trust holding a portfolio of income-producing real estate assets; units listed

explanation.text: The Logic: The source workbook defines REITs as vehicles that pool investor funds into income-generating commercial real estate, distribute earnings to unit-holders, are structured as trusts, and must be listed on stock exchanges. The keyed option reflects all of those source-backed features. The Trap: A direct property purchase is single-asset and not pooled. A commercial loan is debt rather than equity ownership of real estate. A life insurance product is a different product category entirely. Note: Only the trust, income-generating real estate, unit-holder distribution, and listing features are anchored to the cited pages; specific PMS-client suitability or distribution-yield ranges require a separately cited source.
